facts: 2026-09-01: Claude Code changelog v2.1.253 (post v2.1.251): 'Fixed file tools following symlinks swapped after permission check, risking unauthorized access' — a TOCTOU symlink-swap vulnerability in file tools.

2026-09-01: Gemini CLI v0.58.0 stable release notes: 'Enforced consistent symlink evaluation in ignore path handling to prevent path bypass' and 'Isolated Docker and container runtime sockets and binaries in macOS Seatbelt to restrict unauthorized container execution access'.
Claude Code v2.1.259: 'Fixed Bash Read() deny rules not covering files given as option values or operands' — deny rules were bypassable by passing protected files as command options/operands.

Claude Code v2.1.260: 'Fixed Edit/Write/Read rules with parentheses in path being dropped or ignored by sandbox'; 'Fixed one uncompilable file permission pattern failing all file edits; such rules now guard'; 'Fixed Bash auto-approving zsh commands hiding command substitution in specific variable assignments'.

Codex CLI 0.151.0 (2026-08-29): 'Prevented stale Guardian classifications from authorizing actions after permission [changes]' — stale approval classifications could authorize actions after the permission profile changed.

Codex CLI 0.153.0 (2026-09-03): 'Guardian review history survives compaction, restarts, and user-created forks' — before this fix, approval/review history was lost across compaction, restart, and fork; also 'Full Access skips Guardian reviews for confirmation-only actions'.

Codex CLI 0.152.0 (2026-09-01): 'Automatic approval reviews preserve user instructions, answers, and valid [context]' — automatic approval reviews previously dropped user instructions and answers. 0.152.1 (2026-09-01): 'Guardian approval review now honors Node REPL policies provided through model [config]'.

Claude Code v2.1.257: 'Fixed sessions dispatched from agent view overriding target directory's permission mode'; v2.1.258: 'Fixed remote/scheduled sessions failing after re-sent permission approval couldn't be applied'.

Anthropic Claude Platform release notes 2026-09-01 (Claude Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1): 'tool_choice types any and tool aren't supported and return a 400 error'; 'Thinking blocks produced by Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are preserved only for the model that produced them or a newer one: earlier models can't read them, and the API drops one replayed to an earlier model'; 'for new accounts created on or after August 31, 2026, replaying one after the system prompt, tools, or an earlier message changed returns a 400 error'.

Claude Code v2.1.254: 'Fixed Opus 5 requests failing when effort was xhigh/max with thinking disabled' — harness-level breakage from the same model-generation parameter-validity divergence (platform docs: 'thinking: {"type": "disabled"} with effort xhigh or max returns a 400 error').

GitHub changelog 2026-09-02/2026-09-04: 'Copilot app and CLI now honor content exclusions, keeping sensitive code out of context across agentic workflows' (content exclusions moved to GA in Copilot app/CLI) — implying agentic surfaces previously did not enforce org content-exclusion policy.

Claude Code v2.1.253: 'Fixed project settings enabling detailed tracing or raw API body logging without proper controls' — repository-checked project settings could turn on raw API body logging; and 'Fixed plugin commands able to point outside plugin directory; such paths now rejected' (plugin path traversal).

Claude Code v2.1.259: 'Fixed concurrent sessions silently reverting each other's ~/.claude.json changes' — parallel sessions clobbered shared user config (related to existing P-20260831-C476A122 shared-infrastructure isolation family; noted as fact, not separate candidate).

Claude Code v2.1.255: 'Fixed prompt-cache miss roughly hourly in long sessions from tool definition re-rendering' — nondeterministic tool-definition rendering silently broke prompt caching and inflated cost (relates to K06; provider fixed).

Gemini CLI v0.59.0-preview.0 (2026-09-01): 'Prevented Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in Model Context Protocol (MCP) OAuth metadata discovery and authentication' (fixed pre-stable; single provider; fact only).

Codex CLI 0.150.0 (2026-08-26, lookback context): 'Untrusted projects no longer supply project-level AGENTS.md instructions' — matches existing P-20260831-044EBDC6 (workspace trust gating AGENTS.md), already cataloged; no material change beyond the fix already in scope.

2026-09-01: Claude Fable 5.1 launched (Claude API/Bedrock/GCP/Foundry); 2026-09-04: GPT-6 Astra GA in GitHub Copilot and became Codex CLI bundled default (0.153.4); Gemini 3.8 Flash rolling out in Copilot — three concurrent default-model shifts in one week across coding-agent products (context for K02/D02/D14 monitoring, not a new problem).
inferences: Two providers independently shipped symlink-resolution fixes in the same week (Claude Code 2.1.253 TOCTOU symlink swap; Gemini CLI 0.58.0 ignore-path symlink bypass), indicating symlink-based divergence between permission/ignore-check-time path resolution and access-time resolution is a recurring cross-product mechanism, distinct from cataloged shell-bypass (P-20260831-AE8A3EE7) and allowlist-parsing (P-20260831-60EFB5BF) problems.

Codex Guardian fixes (0.151.0, 0.152.0, 0.153.0) plus Claude Code 2.1.257/2.1.258 form a cross-provider pattern: approval/review state is not kept consistent with session lifecycle events (compaction, restart, fork, permission-profile change, cross-context dispatch), failing both open (stale approvals authorize) and closed (valid approvals lost).

Anthropic's Fable/Mythos 5.1 changes make API parameter validity and conversation-replay validity model-generation-scoped (tool_choice 400s, thinking-block downgrade drops, prefix-invariance 400s), so harnesses that switch or fall back between models mid-session, or that edit system/tools mid-conversation, can break without any caller-side change — adjacent to but mechanically distinct from P-20260831-DE8D86E9 (beta→GA/SDK-major breakage).

records.summary: Two providers fixed the same mechanism in the same week. Claude Code v2.1.253 (early Sept 2026): 'Fixed file tools following symlinks swapped after permission check, risking unauthorized access' — a time-of-check/time-of-use gap where a path is approved, then the symlink is swapped so the file tool operates on a different target. Gemini CLI v0.58.0 (2026-09-01): 'Enforced consistent symlink evaluation in ignore path handling to prevent path bypass' — ignore/exclusion paths evaluated inconsistently against symlinks allowed bypassing protections. Codex CLI 0.151.0 (2026-08-29) similarly 'Improved remote sandbox enforcement using the executor's actual home directory', a path-resolution mismatch between policy and executor. Mechanism: permission/ignore decisions are made on a lexical or check-time path while the filesystem operation resolves symlinks at use time, so protected files are reachable (or protections silently skipped) through approved-looking paths. Distinct from shell-based bypass (P-20260831-AE8A3EE7) and allowlist string-parsing mismatch (P-20260831-60EFB5BF): here the checker and executor disagree on filesystem path identity.

records.summary: Cross-provider cluster of fixes (2026-08-29 → 2026-09-03) showing that agent approval/review state is not kept consistent with session lifecycle events, failing both open and closed. Fail-open: Codex CLI 0.151.0 (2026-08-29) 'Prevented stale Guardian classifications from authorizing actions after permission [changes]' — a cached approval classification kept authorizing actions after the permission profile changed; Claude Code v2.1.257 'Fixed sessions dispatched from agent view overriding target directory's permission mode' — dispatch context carried the wrong permission mode into a target directory. Fail-closed/lost state: Codex 0.153.0 (2026-09-03) 'Guardian review history survives compaction, restarts, and user-created forks' — review history was previously lost on compaction, restart, and fork; Codex 0.152.0 (2026-09-01) 'Automatic approval reviews preserve user instructions, answers, and valid [context]' — automated reviews dropped the user's instructions and prior answers; Claude Code v2.1.258 'Fixed remote/scheduled sessions failing after re-sent permission approval couldn't be applied'. Mechanism: approval decisions are stored as session-local ephemeral state with no invalidation/persistence contract tied to permission-profile changes, context compaction, restarts, forks, or cross-context dispatch — so security review either re-authorizes stale decisions or silently loses valid ones, and users cannot tell which regime they are in.

records.summary: With Claude Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 (2026-09-01), parameter validity and conversation-replay validity became model-generation-scoped: 'tool_choice types any and tool aren't supported and return a 400 error' (harnesses forcing tool use break on model upgrade with no caller change); 'Thinking blocks... are preserved only for the model that produced them or a newer one: earlier models can't read them, and the API drops one replayed to an earlier model' (silent content drop on model downgrade/fallback mid-conversation — the exact path overload fallbacks take); 'for new accounts created on or after August 31, 2026, replaying one after the system prompt, tools, or an earlier message changed returns a 400 error' (hard failure for harnesses that edit system prompts/tools mid-session, e.g. compaction, dynamic tool registration, turn-scoped instructions — and account-creation-date-conditional, so behavior differs across accounts running identical code). Related earlier instance: Opus 5 rejects thinking-disabled at effort xhigh/max (Claude Code itself shipped the client-side fix in v2.1.254). Mechanism: the same API version now enforces per-model-generation and per-account-cohort semantics, so mid-session model switching, fallback, and history/prompt mutation — standard coding-agent harness techniques — become version-skew failure surfaces. Adjacent to P-20260831-DE8D86E9 (beta→GA/SDK-major silent breakage) but the trigger is model selection, not API/SDK version; evaluate merge vs new at merge gate.

records.summary: Enterprise data-governance policies are enforced on older product surfaces but silently unenforced on newer agentic ones until later patched. GitHub changelog 2026-09-02/2026-09-04: 'Copilot app and CLI now honor content exclusions, keeping sensitive code out of context across agentic workflows' — content exclusions reached GA in Copilot app/CLI only in this window, implying agentic workflows previously pulled excluded (sensitive) code into model context despite org policy configured for the IDE surfaces. Same-week sibling in Claude Code v2.1.253: 'Fixed project settings enabling detailed tracing or raw API body logging without proper controls' — repository-checked project settings could enable raw API body logging (prompts, code, potentially secrets written to logs) without the control gates that govern such telemetry. Mechanism: policy enforcement (exclusions, telemetry controls) is implemented per-surface, and fast-shipping agent surfaces launch before inheriting it, creating a window where admins believe policy applies but the agent surface ignores it. Related to I05/I06/I14 as impact, but the mechanism (per-surface policy-enforcement lag) is not separately cataloged. Medium confidence: prior non-enforcement is implied by the GA wording, not documented as an advisory.
